root_cause: Observed two READY Netlify production deployments with provider commit_ref=null whose release.json contained 40-hex values that GitHub could not resolve as Bedrijfsgeheugen commits. A possible contributing source flaw is that netlify-build-entry.mjs restamps release.json from transient git rev-parse HEAD after the canonical release-evidence phase already wrote a source-derived identity; the precise provider writer/build origin requires production build-log corroboration.
remediation: Use the original release-source-identity resolver to bind the final restamp to the already generated release-evidence source commit, validated against provider COMMIT_REF and/or .bg-source-commit. Where neither provider COMMIT_REF nor source marker exists, permit HEAD-only native fallback only with the canonical GitHub origin plus equal checked-out HEAD and origin/main; otherwise fail closed before deployment. Keep the same Netlify native Git/controlled OIDC transport, protected PR, source lane, reviewer and workflow.
prevention: tests/brain-netlify-final-source-identity-attestation-20261105.test.mjs verifies real-provider vs source-marker vs synthetic Git HEAD/mismatch/legitimate native Git remote. Never declare live until exact protected main, READY provider and independently matching canonical + immutable release.json plus original browser proof.
open_obligations: Exact-head Required, CodeQL, BRAIN and Netlify build parity must succeed
Protected merge and native/current production deployment with independent canonical+immutable release.json readback
Owner root-cause attribution from Netlify build and Git workflow logs for unverified deploy writer
Natural subsequent run must demonstrate no recurrence across API and Git-native paths
Portal human usability, two-tenant WCAG and assistive-technology acceptance remain separately open
